summary: Joyful Jack is a pumpkin-head cowboy animatronic that greets people at events: the existing talking head (eyes, eyelids, jaw, a neck that turns and nods) on a legless torso that stands on a concrete-filled bucket, with two motorised arms and simple hands that can wave, point and hold a light object. It runs from Milwaukee M18 tool packs inside the torso and is built in one of three tiers (A Beginner, B Midrange, C Maxed); this package is the tier named on its cover.
features: Stands on its own: a 5 US gal bucket of concrete on a 24 in plywood skirt, a 1 in steel pipe mast, no legs
Two arms on hollow-hub joints (two 6806 bearings each), with spring assist at the shoulder so the servos only carry what the springs do not
Tiers B and C: Feetech serial-bus servos that report position, load and temperature, GT3 belt reductions at the shoulder and elbow
Hands: a one-servo cartoon mitt (A), a two-servo glove hand (B), or Pollen Robotics' eight-servo AmazingHand (C)
Milwaukee M18 packs behind a rear hatch: one pack (A), two packs either of which can be swapped while the other runs (B, C), plus wall power (C)
Protection: low-voltage cutoff, fuses, and an emergency stop that cuts power to every actuator
Printed parts in PETG-CF and PETG with brass heat-set inserts; aluminium 2020 frame (B, C) or birch plywood box (A)

functions.text: Stand upright unattended on a floor and resist being bumped
Move each arm through shoulder flex, shoulder out and elbow (plus upper-arm twist and wrist twist in B and C, wrist pitch in C)
Open and close the hand around a light object
Power the head and both arms from M18 packs for an event, and stop every actuator from the E-stop
Carry the existing head and its electronics on the neck plate

requirements.text: Torso, no legs, standing on a ballasted base on a mast; must not tip when bumped or leaned on (target load TBD: Q4)
requirements.how: Tip test: push at shoulder height with a force gauge, arms out, until the skirt lifts (simulation: research/sim)

requirements.text: Battery and power electronics inside the torso on Milwaukee M18 packs, swappable without removing the costume
requirements.how: Inspection and a pack swap through the rear hatch with the costume on

requirements.text: Runs for extended periods (hours per pack TBD: Q7)
requirements.how: Run test: a gesture loop on one pack, logging pack voltage until the low-voltage cutoff

requirements.text: Two motorised arms with simple character hands that can grasp an object (payload TBD: Q5, assumed 0.25 kg)
requirements.how: Hold a 0.25 kg object at full reach for 60 s; joint loads logged (simulation: research/sim)

requirements.text: Keeps and powers the existing head (Raspberry Pi 4B, PCA9685, neck stepper, camera, audio)
requirements.how: Power-on test of the head from the torso supply

requirements.text: Safe among children: emergency stop, limited speed and grip force, no exposed pinch points, arms settle to a rest pose on power loss
requirements.how: E-stop test under motion; grip force measured on a scale; inspection of the costume over the joints
